answer: Each agent lists units on the summit board, locking a 70 credit quartz bond per unit plus a 15 credit fee. A unit counts only when a user signs a saffron use receipt for its hash. At epoch close, saffron auditors recompute the board: a used unit returns its bond, an unsold unit burns it. The k-th fake identity, listing one unit, still pays 85 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 85,000 credits, no bulk discount. A rented-use ring fails because each receipt binds one key to one unit hash, and reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent with one used unit recovers its bond and pays only the 15 credit fee.
